user.title: SAMDUO Local TCP Control
user.description: Connect to a SAMDUO battery over your local network. The serial number is read from the device automatically. Make sure the 'HEMS Managed' toggle in the SAMDUO app is switched OFF, and note the device answers only one TCP client at a time.

data_description.host: IP address or hostname of the battery (e.g. 192.168.1.95)
data_description.port: TCP port of the local API (default 3335)
data_description.name: Display name for this battery in Home Assistant

zeroconf_confirm.description: Add the {model} at {host} (serial {serial})? Make sure the 'HEMS Managed' toggle in the SAMDUO app is switched OFF before using any control features.

error.cannot_connect: Could not connect to the device. Check the host and port, and make sure nothing else (e.g. the SAMDUO app) is holding the device's only TCP connection.

abort.not_supported: This SAMDUO device is not a supported battery

data_description.host: IP address or hostname of the battery
data_description.port: TCP port of the local API (default 3335)
data_description.name: Display name for this battery in Home Assistant
data_description.poll_interval: How often to poll the battery for new data (default 5)
data_description.max_charge_power: Upper bound for charge commands (default 800, the grid-compliant output; max 2600, the inverter rating - keep it at or below the limit set in the SAMDUO app)
data_description.max_discharge_power: Upper bound for discharge commands (default 800; max 2600 - keep it at or below the limit set in the SAMDUO app)
data_description.keepalive_interval: How often an active setpoint is re-sent to the battery (default 30)
data_description.control_timeout: How long the battery holds a setpoint without a refresh before resuming self-management (default 90; must exceed the keepalive interval)

hems_blocked.title: {device_name} is ignoring power commands
hems_blocked.description:
The battery confirms every power setpoint but its measured power does not follow the commands. This happens when 'HEMS Managed' is switched ON on the battery's Device Settings page in the SAMDUO app (together with 'Self Consumption' in the general home settings): the battery then manages itself using its own P1 meter and silently ignores external commands.

To control the battery from Home Assistant, switch 'HEMS Managed' OFF on the battery's Device Settings page. The inverse also holds: with 'HEMS Managed' OFF the battery does nothing on its own and only acts on commands from Home Assistant.
